title: Roundup: BioMarin Licenses Long-Acting Fabry Enzyme Therapy for $70 Million Upfront, Ferring to Acquire Fertility Biotech Gameto in Deal Worth Up to $1.38 Billion
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 29, 2026 Roundup: BioMarin Licenses Long-Acting Fabry Enzyme Therapy for $70 Million Upfront, Ferring to Acquire Fertility Biotech Gameto in Deal Worth Up to $1.38 Billion Author(s)Pharmaceutical Executive Editorial Staff BioMarin licenses long-acting Fabry enzyme replacement therapy HM15421/GC1134A, while Ferring agrees to acquire fertility biotech Gameto. Advertisement Two deals announced this week show established drugmakers adding specialty assets in very different corners of medicine. BioMarin paid $70 million upfront for exclusive worldwide rights to an investigational long-acting therapy for Fabry disease, with up to $405 million in further milestones.1 Ferring Pharmaceuticals signed an agreement to acquire Gameto, a cell-engineering company focused on women’s reproductive health, in a transaction worth up to $1.3825 billion if development, regulatory and commercial milestones are met.2Key FactsBioMarin: license for HM15421/GC1134A (Fabry)Terms: $70M upfront, up to $405M milestonesHM15421/GC1134A: Phase 1/2, subcutaneous designFerring to acquire Gameto: up to $1.3825BGameto program: investigational in the U.S.Ferring close: pending customary conditionsBioMarin Licenses Long-Acting Enzyme Therapy for Fabry DiseaseBioMarin entered an exclusive worldwide license agreement with GC Biopharma and Hanmi Pharm for HM15421/GC1134A, an investigational, long-acting enzyme replacement therapy for Fabry disease, the company announced Oct. 29.1 BioMarin pays $70 million upfront. GC Biopharma and Hanmi are jointly eligible for up to $405 million in development and commercial milestones, plus tiered royalties on net sales; the royalty rates were not disclosed.1“This agreement reflects our growing commitment to the Fabry community, building on the acquisition of Amicus earlier this year,” says Alexander Hardy, president and chief executive officer of BioMarin.Following the ongoing Phase 1/2 study, BioMarin assumes sole responsibility for clinical development, manufacturing and commercialization outside Korea, where GC Biopharma and Hanmi retain commercialization rights.1 The release does not say who funds the current study, and it gives no closing conditions or timeline.1What is HM15421/GC1134A?The candidate is a human recombinant alpha-galactosidase A enzyme designed for a longer half-life and better stability, features intended to support subcutaneous dosing. BioMarin says it has the potential to be the first subcutaneous enzyme replacement therapy for Fabry disease.1 (()=>{var l=(n,t)=>{let i=async()=>{await(await n())()},e=typeof t.value=="object"?t.value:void 0,s={timeout:e==null?void 0:e.timeout};"requestIdleCallback"in window?window.requestIdleCallback(i,s):setTimeout(i,s.timeout||200)};(self.Astro||(self.Astro={})).idle=l;window.dispatchEvent(new Event("astro:idle"));})(); The company reports differentiated preclinical efficacy in renal function, vascular health and peripheral nervous system outcomes, and FDA granted the candidate orphan drug designation in 2024.1 Hardy says HM15421/GC1134A is “an excellent fit and could allow us to reach a new generation of patients with Fabry.”What unmet need does the program target?Fabry disease is an X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by changes in the GLA gene. Reduced alpha-galactosidase A activity allows globotriaosylceramide to build up in cells, which is believed to drive symptoms that include pain, kidney failure and increased risk of heart attack and stroke. Symptoms can be severe, vary between patients and begin early in life.1 A published review reported an annual incidence of 1 in 100,000 and cautioned that this may underestimate true prevalence.3What remains unproven?The program is in an early-stage trial, and the release reports no clinical efficacy or safety results. The efficacy claims cited so far are preclinical and company-reported, and whether a subcutaneous formulation improves outcomes for patients has not been tested.1Ferring to Acquire Fertility Biotech GametoFerring signed an agreement on Oct. 27 to acquire Gameto, a biotechnology company that uses cell engineering for women’s reproductive health, starting with infertility and expanding into ovarian disease and menopause.2 The transaction is worth up to $1.3825 billion, with payments contingent on development, regulatory and commercial milestones. The upfront payment was not disclosed.2,4 Completion is subject to customary and other closing conditions, and the companies will operate independently until then. No closing date was given.2“Ferring has been committed to helping people build families for more than 50 years,” says Jean-Frédéric Paulsen, chairman of the board and chief executive officer of Ferring Pharmaceuticals. “By combining Gameto’s scientific innovation with our expertise and global reproductive-medicine platform, we see an opportunity to advance new approaches in fertility care and reach more patients worldwide.”What is Gameto developing?Ferring’s release states that Gameto’s egg-maturation program is investigational in the U.S. and has not been approved by FDA.2 BioPharma Dive reports that the lead product, Fertilo, uses stem cell-derived ovarian support cells to grow eggs outside the body, is in Phase 3 testing in the U.S., and is cleared for use in Australia and parts of Latin America. Gameto says the approach could remove the need for hormone injections and shorten fertility treatment cycles to “as little as three days.” The company has raised $127 million since its 2020 founding.4“This is a defining moment for Gameto and for our mission to transform reproductive health,” says Dina Turner, PhD, chief executive officer and co-founder of Gameto. “By combining our pioneering cell-engineering platform with Ferring’s deep expertise and global reach, we have an extraordinary opportunity to accelerate innovation, expand access and bring more modern fertility treatment options to women and families around the world.”What questions remain about the deal?The size of the upfront payment, the expected closing date and the share of the $1.3825 billion tied to regulatory milestones were not disclosed.2,4SourcesBioMarin enters into exclusive worldwide license agreement with GC Biopharma and Hanmi Pharm for investigational next-generation enzyme replacement therapy, adding a second potential treatment for Fabry disease. title: Lilly shuffles business structure; Novartis writes off part of Avidity deal
content: An article from News roundup Lilly shuffles business structure; Novartis writes off part of Avidity deal Lilly intends to merge its U.S. and international divisions when a top executive retires. Elsewhere, Astellas closed in on what it believes to be a “best-in-class” cancer immunotherapy prospect. Published Oct. 28, 2026 By BioPharma Dive staff Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Getty Images Today, a brief rundown of news involving Eli Lilly and Novartis, as well as updates from Astellas Pharma, Pfizer and Bolt Biotherapeutics that you may have missed. Patrik Jonsson will retire from Eli Lilly at the end of 2026, completing a 36-year run at the Indianapolis-based drugmaker. Jonsson started at Lilly as a sales representative in Sweden in 1990 and rose through the ranks to eventually lead the company’s global pharmaceutical business, “Lilly International.” Once he steps down, Lilly’s U.S. and international divisions will combine into an entity called “Lilly Global Markets” and be headed by Ilya Yuffa, a Lilly executive vice president and head of global customer capabilities. title: Roundup: Astellas Licenses IL-12 Fusion Protein From Audax in Deal Worth Up to $1.34 Billion, EVERSANA Acquires Health Economics Firm Estima Scientific
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 28, 2026 Roundup: Astellas Licenses IL-12 Fusion Protein From Audax in Deal Worth Up to $1.34 Billion, EVERSANA Acquires Health Economics Firm Estima Scientific Author(s)Pharmaceutical Executive Editorial Staff Astellas gains an option on Audax’s IL-12 antibody-cytokine fusion DAX-044, while EVERSANA acquires London-based health economics firm Estima Scientific. Advertisement Two transactions announced this week sit at opposite ends of the biopharma value chain: access to an early-stage immuno-oncology program, and the technology used to show payers what a product is worth. Astellas Pharma Inc. secured an exclusive option on an investigational cancer therapy from Audax Biosciences Pty Ltd, in a deal valued at up to US$1.34 billion excluding royalties.1 EVERSANA, a commercial services provider to the biopharmaceutical industry, acquired Estima Scientific, a London-based health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) technology company, for undisclosed terms.2Key FactsAstellas–Audax: option and license for DAX-044DAX-044: IL-12 antibody-cytokine fusionValue: up to US$1.34B, excluding royaltiesPhase 1 expected to begin in 2027EVERSANA acquires London-based Estima ScientificEstima: generative AI tools for HEOREVERSANA deal terms: not disclosedAstellas Gains Option on Audax’s IL-12 Antibody-Cytokine FusionAstellas and Audax, an Australian biotechnology company, entered an exclusive option and license agreement for DAX-044, an investigational, immune-targeted interleukin-12 (IL-12) antibody-cytokine fusion for immuno-oncology.1 “By combining Audax’s innovative science with Astellas’ development, manufacturing and commercialization expertise, we hope to advance a potential new treatment option for patients with solid tumors, including cancers where effective immune stimulation remains an important therapeutic challenge,” says Takahiko Iwaya, chief strategy officer at Astellas.If Astellas exercises the option, it would receive a worldwide license to develop, manufacture and commercialize DAX-044 and assume sole responsibility for those activities. Audax has the option to co-fund and co-promote the drug in Australia and New Zealand. Exercise is subject to customary conditions, including antitrust clearances.1 Total potential value reaches up to US$1.34 billion, excluding royalties. Audax would receive US$285 million through an upfront payment and a potential option exercise payment, plus up to US$1.05 billion in development and commercial milestones and tiered double-digit royalties on worldwide net sales if the drug is approved.1 Audax will fund and continue development into a Phase 1 study expected to begin in 2027.1Why has IL-12 been difficult to develop as a cancer therapy?DAX-044 uses the AVIKINE antibody-cytokine platform and is designed to concentrate IL-12’s immune-activating activity in the tumor microenvironment while limiting the systemic toxicity that has historically constrained IL-12-based therapy.1 That constraint is documented. Audax says preclinical studies show a potentially best-in-class therapeutic index for an IL-12 agent, a characterization the company has not yet tested in patients.1 Audax also cautions that Astellas may not exercise its option and that milestone payments may never be received.1“DAX-044 is a promising investigational immuno-oncology program with a differentiated mechanism designed to selectively activate anti-tumor immune responses,” Iwaya says.Jai Rautela, PhD, MBA, chief executive officer of Audax, frames the deal around the clinical timeline. “This partnership will expedite the planned phase 1 clinical evaluation of DAX-044 for the benefit of patients with various types of solid tumor,” he says.EVERSANA Acquires Health Economics Firm Estima ScientificEVERSANA has acquired Estima Scientific, a London-based HEOR technology and services company founded in 2019. Financial terms were not disclosed.2 Estima pairs specialist consulting with proprietary software, including web-based generative artificial intelligence (AI) applications for economic modeling, systematic literature reviews and network meta-analysis.2 Its team, including co-founders Tim Reason and Andy Gimblett, will join EVERSANA’s global workforce, and its expertise will be folded into EVERSANA’s market access and value and evidence solutions, with continuity planned for existing clients.2How are health technology assessment bodies treating AI?HEOR work supports the evidence manufacturers submit to payers and to health technology assessment bodies. The release says Estima’s solutions have been validated by large pharmaceutical customers and by assessment bodies, including the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE), but it does not describe what that validation covered.2 NICE’s August 2024 position statement says any use of AI should follow the principle of “augmentation, not replacement, of human involvement,” and that the submitting organization remains accountable for the content of its submission.4“The company’s global scale and end-to-end commercial infrastructure will allow us to accelerate how pharmaceutical companies build and communicate evidence-based value to payers, helping patients gain faster access to life-changing therapies,” says Reason, co-founder of Estima Scientific.What is the strategic rationale?The deal builds on EVERSANA’s AI Agency platform, launched in 2025 and expanded in August 2026.2 “As we scale to serve global clients, adding best-in-class companies that embrace a technology first mindset is critical to our success. The Estima Scientific team checks every box and will seamlessly fit into our organization,” says Mark Thierer, CEO of EVERSANA.Because the price and integration timeline were not disclosed, the transaction’s financial scale and its effect on Estima’s existing client contracts remain unclear.2SourcesAstellas and Audax Biosciences enter exclusive option and license agreement for DAX-044, a novel immune-targeted IL-12 antibody-cytokine fusion for immuno-oncology. content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 15, 2026 AstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 Billion Author(s)Pharmaceutical Executive Editorial Staff AstraZeneca will pay insitro $40 million upfront to apply AI to target discovery in MASH and cardiomyopathies, with no candidates named yet. Advertisement AstraZeneca has signed a drug discovery collaboration and licensing agreement with insitro to apply artificial intelligence (AI) to target identification and therapeutic design in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and cardiomyopathies, the companies announced Oct. 15.1,2 Insitro will receive $40 million upfront and is eligible for up to approximately $1.46 billion in milestones.1,2Sharon Barr, executive vice president and head of BioPharmaceuticals research and development at AstraZeneca, tied the agreement to target selection: “We know that disease biology is incredibly complex, and one of the most critical decisions in R&D is selecting the right target. This strategic collaboration underscores our commitment to maximizing the potential of cutting-edge AI to tackle the root cause of disease. Partnering with insitro, we will use advanced AI to identify the biological drivers of disease to support the rapid discovery of high-quality novel targets, advancing our ambition to deliver the next generation of medicines to patients faster.”1“MASH and cardiomyopathies are prevalent, underdiagnosed diseases where high-content data holds immense potential for uncovering disease drivers. By applying AI to these complex datasets, we can unlock greater discovery power and reveal novel genetic insights.”What are AstraZeneca and insitro agreeing to do?Insitro will use its Virtual Human platform to identify causal disease biology in both indications and advance AstraZeneca-nominated targets from discovery to development candidate.1,2 The platform combines large-scale human and cellular data with AI-enabled target identification and medicine design.1AstraZeneca will take the clinical development and regulatory work and holds exclusive worldwide rights to the selected programs; insitro’s release adds that AstraZeneca will also lead commercialization.1,2Beyond the upfront payment, insitro is eligible for single-digit royalties on global sales.1,2 The two releases describe the milestones slightly differently: AstraZeneca cites development and commercial milestones, while insitro includes discovery milestones.1,2The upfront payment represents less than 3% of the combined headline value, and neither company disclosed the number of targets, program timelines or payment schedule.Why are MASH and cardiomyopathies difficult to treat?Insitro’s release says each disease is defined by heterogeneity, with a single diagnostic label covering patients whose underlying biology differs, which has complicated treatment.2 (()=>{var l=(n,t)=>{let i=async()=>{await(await n())()},e=typeof t.value=="object"?t.value:void 0,s={timeout:e==null?void 0:e.timeout};"requestIdleCallback"in window?window.requestIdleCallback(i,s):setTimeout(i,s.timeout||200)};(self.Astro||(self.Astro={})).idle=l;window.dispatchEvent(new Event("astro:idle"));})(); Daphne Koller, Ph.D., founder and CEO of insitro, said: “MASH and cardiomyopathies are prevalent, underdiagnosed diseases where high-content data holds immense potential for uncovering disease drivers. By applying AI to these complex datasets, we can unlock greater discovery power and reveal novel genetic insights. Our platform simultaneously deconvolutes disease biology and identifies causal drivers of disease pathologies. Partnering with AstraZeneca allows us to pair our deep biological precision with their pharmaceutical expertise and scale with potential for accelerated advancement of novel programs through development and to patients.”2In MASH, the treatment landscape has changed recently. The FDA approved resmetirom (Rezdiffra) in March 2024 under its accelerated approval pathway for adults with noncirrhotic disease and moderate to advanced liver scarring, to be used with diet and exercise. The agency, which at the time referred to the condition as nonalcoholic steatohepatitis, said patients had previously lacked a medication that directly addressed their liver damage, and cited an estimate of 6 million to 8 million U.S. patients at that disease stage.3The cardiomyopathy picture is less defined in the releases, which do not specify which forms are in scope. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, the most common inherited cardiovascular disorder, is estimated to affect 1 in 500 people, and a published review notes that existing studies may have underestimated its prevalence.4 That offers one illustration of the underdiagnosis Koller describes, though it should not be read as the collaboration’s target population.How does the collaboration fit each company’s portfolio?AstraZeneca describes cardiovascular, renal and metabolism as one of its main disease areas and a key growth driver, with an emphasis on the links among the heart, kidneys, liver and pancreas.1 A program spanning a liver disease and heart muscle diseases fits within that framing.Insitro says it has built a multimodal corpus of human and cellular data since 2018 and is advancing nine programs, including genetic regulators of liver fat and fibrosis expected to enter the clinic in early 2027.2 The company reports more than $750 million in capital and existing collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb, Lilly and Gilead.2 The release does not say how its internal liver programs relate to targets AstraZeneca will nominate.What remains unknown about the collaboration?No candidate, efficacy data or safety data accompany the announcement, and the collaboration sits at the discovery stage. Targets identified through AI-driven analysis of human data will still need validation through preclinical work and clinical trials, where heterogeneity of disease could also affect trial design. Milestone and royalty figures are potential payments contingent on progress that neither company has timed publicly. Neither release addresses market reaction, and independent verification of the platform’s performance in these indications was not available at the time of publication.SourcesAstraZeneca announces new strategic collaboration with insitro to use advanced AI systems to develop transformative therapeutics for difficult to treat cardiometabolic diseases. 10月28日，恒瑞医药发布2026年第三季度报告。第三季度，公司实现营业收入89.53亿元，同比增长20.55%；归母净利润24.58亿元，同比增长88.92%；利润总额27.76亿元，同比增长103.97%。前三季度，公司实现营业收入244.09亿元，归母净利润69.23亿元，同比增长20.38%。图源：恒瑞医药2026年第三季度报告业绩增长的同时，恒瑞医药创新药业务也有新进展。CDE官网同日公示，公司自主研发的ADC药物瑞康曲妥珠单抗一项新适应症上市申请获受理。结合该药此前的临床研究及审评进展，此次申报可能涉及HER2阳性复发或转移性乳腺癌一线治疗，具体适应症仍需以官方披露为准。一、创新药销售超138亿元，对外授权持续贡献收入从前三季度经营情况来看，创新药已成为恒瑞医药收入的重要组成部分。2026年前三季度，公司创新药销售收入达138.71亿元，同比增长17.05%，占药品销售收入的比重提升至64.59%。其中，抗肿瘤创新产品收入98.65亿元，同比增长3.13%，占创新药销售收入的71.12%；非肿瘤创新产品收入40.06亿元，同比增长75.36%，占比达到28.88%。图源：整合于恒瑞医药2026年第三季度报告除产品销售外，创新药对外许可业务也为公司带来收入增量。前三季度，恒瑞医药创新药对外许可业务确认收入27.81亿元，同比增长31.12%，主要来自GSK、BMS相关合作的进度确认收入，以及个别已授权产品的里程碑款。同期，公司收到对外许可合作首付款及里程碑款现金共43.43亿元，主要包括BMS支付的6亿美元首付款。第三季度单季确认许可收入约13.6亿元，这类收入具有较高毛利率。在已授权项目持续贡献收入的同时，恒瑞医药也在拓展新的海外合作。2026年9月，公司与诺和诺德达成协议，将每周一次口服给药的GLP-1/GIP双受体激动剂HRS-1596有偿许可给诺和诺德，授予其大中华地区以外全球范围内的开发、生产和商业化独家权利。该交易潜在总金额最高可达26亿美元，包括3亿美元首付款，以及后续开发、注册和商业化里程碑付款及销售提成。另一条出海路径是NewCo模式。8月6日，恒瑞医药的合作伙伴Braveheart Bio登陆美国纳斯达克。此前，恒瑞将自主研发的心肌肌球蛋白小分子抑制剂HRS-1893有偿许可给Braveheart Bio，并获得该公司部分股权。这是继今年4月Kailera Therapeutics登陆纳斯达克后，恒瑞医药NewCo模式取得的又一进展。二、多款创新药上市申请获受理，研发管线持续推进销售与授权业务之外，创新药研发及上市申报进展同样值得关注。2026年第三季度，恒瑞医药共有7项上市申请获CDE受理，其中GLP-1相关产品取得多项进展。企业公告+摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库整合具体来看，口服GLP-1受体激动剂HRS-7535片用于成人2型糖尿病患者血糖控制、成人长期体重管理的两项上市申请均获受理；GLP-1/GIP双受体激动剂瑞普泊肽注射液用于成人2型糖尿病患者血糖控制的上市申请也获受理。从产品储备来看，截至目前，恒瑞医药已有27款1类创新药和6款2类新药在中国获批上市，另有100多个自主创新产品处于临床开发阶段，400余项临床试验在国内外开展。多款产品推进上市申报，也为公司后续创新药商业化提供了新的观察窗口。 title: 科伦博泰B7-H3 ADC药物SKB500联合PD-1/VEGF双抗获批临床，经治SCLC患者有望解锁更优治疗方案
content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 注册审批 科伦博泰B7-H3 ADC药物SKB500联合PD-1/VEGF双抗获批临床，经治SCLC患者有望解锁更优治疗方案 科伦博泰B7-H3 ADC药物SKB500联合PD-1/VEGF双抗获批临床，经治SCLC患者有望解锁更优治疗方案 张鹏 · 新药研发分析师 张 张鹏 新药研发分析师 审核：王正晴 · 药学博士 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 昨天 10:35 2005 CD276 PD-1 VEGF 小细胞肺癌 芦康沙妥珠单抗 10月26日，CDE官网显示，科伦博泰自主研发的B7-H3 ADC药物SKB500联合PD-1/VEGF双抗SKB118，用于小细胞肺癌（SCLC）患者的Ⅱ期临床试验申请获批。图源：CDE官网此次联用将B7-H3 ADC与同时靶向PD-1、VEGF通路的双抗相结合，进一步探索ADC联合免疫治疗在SCLC中的应用潜力。一、SKB500Ⅰ期数据公布，ORR最高达75%SKB500是一款科伦博泰自主研发的B7-H3 ADC，采用高亲和力、高亲水性及内吞作用更强的抗体，并通过可裂解的亲水性AAA连接子连接载荷，药物抗体比（DAR）约为8。2026年ESMO大会上，科伦博泰公布了SKB500治疗广泛期小细胞肺癌（ES-SCLC）的Ⅰ期研究数据。扩展队列共纳入61例既往接受过系统治疗的患者，所有患者均接受过含铂治疗，其中85.2%接受过PD-(L)1抑制剂治疗。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库截至2026年9月16日，12 mg/kg组和16 mg/kg组的中位随访时间分别为9.3个月和8.3个月，关键数据如下：客观缓解率（ORR）：分别为75.0%和66.7%。中位无进展生存期（mPFS）：分别为8.1个月和5.6个月。中位总生存期（mOS）：分别为14.0个月和10.6个月。安全性：两组≥3级治疗相关不良事件（TRAE）发生率分别为52.5%和66.7%，常见不良事件包括血液学毒性和胃肠道毒性，未报告治疗相关死亡。上述结果来自早期临床研究，后续仍需进一步验证。二、联合PD-1/VEGF双抗，拓展ADC联用策略SKB118（CR-001）由科伦博泰与Crescent联合开发，可同时靶向PD-1和VEGF通路，目前已在中国和美国启动单药Ⅰ期临床试验。此前，科伦博泰已推进SKB118与TROP2 ADC芦康沙妥珠单抗（sac-TMT）的联合开发。此次SKB500与SKB118的联用临床申请获批，进一步拓展了公司在ADC与双抗联合治疗领域的布局。同类联合方案也在持续探索。今年WCLC期间，BNT324/DB-1311联合PD-L1/VEGF双抗Pumitamig治疗肺癌的Ⅰb/Ⅱ期研究公布数据。在71例SCLC患者中，ORR为70.4%；按治疗线数划分，一线、二线及三线及以上患者的ORR分别为92.3%、77.3%和52.4%。这一研究为ADC联合PD-(L)1/VEGF双抗治疗SCLC提供了进一步的临床探索依据，但不同研究的患者人群和设计存在差异，相关数据不宜直接比较。三、多款创新药推进临床，研发管线持续拓展科伦博泰持续推进创新药研发。截至目前，科伦博泰已有3款1类新药获批上市，包括注射用芦康沙妥珠单抗、塔戈利单抗注射液和注射用博度曲妥珠单抗。图源：摩熵医药-中国药品审评数据库此外，科伦药业（含子公司）有超30款1类新药处于获批IND及以上阶段，涉及抗肿瘤药物、神经系统药物、系统用抗感染药物等疾病领域。 MADRID — A personalized mRNA cancer vaccine reduced the risk of disease recurrence in patients with melanoma by 42% compared to a standard treatment, according to a large clinical trial conducted by the drugmakers Moderna and Merck. The results are an important advance for the treatment of melanoma, oncologists said, because patients lived significantly longer without their cancer returning. Advertisement The success of the Moderna-Merck vaccine, intismeran autogene, may also usher in a new wave of treatments for other types of cancer, though experts are debating how broadly applicable the technology could be. The medicine is an individualized therapy that attacks the unique mutations, called neoantigens, found in a patient’s tumor. title: 诺诚健华Q3营收大增150.60%：BD里程碑收入推高业绩，奥布替尼独挑商业化大梁
content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 时讯 诺诚健华Q3营收大增150.60%：BD里程碑收入推高业绩，奥布替尼独挑商业化大梁 诺诚健华Q3营收大增150.60%：BD里程碑收入推高业绩，奥布替尼独挑商业化大梁 李明轩 · 医药投融资分析师 李 李明轩 医药投融资分析师 审核：孙浩 · 特许金融分析师（CFA） 聚焦创新药投融资、小核酸药物与代谢疾病赛道；长期跟踪国内 Biotech 融资动态与管线进展。累计发布原创分析 200+ 篇。 20小时前 1257 北京诺诚健华医药科技有限公司 奥布替尼 2026年Q3 企业营收 BD交易 药品销售增速与整体营收增速之间的明显差距，主要来自BD里程碑收入的确认。诺诚健华（688428.SH/09969.HK）第三季度营业收入同比大增150.60%。但同期药品销售收入增速为38.59%。两组数据出现明显剪刀差，内生盈利能力引发市场关注。10月26日，诺诚健华发布2026年第三季度报告显示，前三季度，公司实现营业收入20.99亿元，同比增长88.21%；归属于上市公司股东的净利润6.56亿元，扣除非经常性损益后的净利润为5.86亿元，实现持续盈利；经营活动产生的现金流量净额为2.20亿元，同比由负转正。图源：诺诚健华官网从增长动因看，除奥布替尼持续放量、坦昔妥单抗和佐来曲替尼新增销售贡献外，诺诚健华与Zenas BioPharma（下称“Zenas”）的授权许可合作完成后续里程碑交付，成为营收增长的重要因素。另一方面，公司单品依赖问题仍较为突出。奥布替尼作为公司商业化收入的核心支柱，仍面临激烈竞争。在27日的业绩说明会上，以诺诚健华首席财务官傅欣为代表的部分高管，一方面坦承BD收入成为公司业绩核心助推力量；另一方面也表示，公司正在着手通过坦昔妥单抗、佐来曲替尼等产品强化公司的商业化盈利能力。一、BD里程碑收入助推单季净利扭亏诺诚健华成立于2015年，是一家处于商业化阶段的生物医药高科技公司，专注于恶性肿瘤及自身免疫性疾病领域一类新药的研发。公司于2020年3月在港交所上市，2022年9月登陆上交所科创板，并于2025年首次实现年度盈利。从单季度表现看，诺诚健华2026年第三季度实现营业收入9.62亿元，同比增长150.60%；归母净利润约4.09亿元，同比扭亏。公司在三季报中解释称，营收增长主要来自奥布替尼持续放量、坦昔妥单抗和佐来曲替尼新增销售贡献，以及与Zenas授权许可协议完成后续里程碑交付。不过，进一步拆分收入结构可以看到，公司整体营收增速明显快于药品销售增速。三季报显示，前三季度公司药品销售收入为14.49亿元，同比增长41.47%，而营业收入同比增长88.21%；单季度看，第三季度药品销售收入为5.31亿元，同比增长38.59%，而营业收入同比增长150.60%。药品销售增速与整体营收增速之间的明显差距，主要来自BD里程碑收入的确认。诺诚健华首席财务官傅欣在27日召开的业绩说明会上表示，扣除药品销售收入后的其余营业收入，主要是公司与Zenas达成的独家许可协议所实现的里程碑收入。回溯来看，2025年10月，诺诚健华子公司InnoCare US与Zenas签署授权协议，将奥布替尼、IL-17抑制剂和TYK2抑制剂在协议约定区域内的相关权益授予Zenas。2026年以来，相关交易对价陆续兑现：上半年公司已确认与IL-17抑制剂对外许可首付款相关收入；8月，InnoCare US又达成与奥布替尼相关的近期里程碑，有权获得Zenas 200万股普通股及2500万美元现金。在此背景下，BD收入对当期营收形成明显推升，而药品销售能否在覆盖相关费用后独立支撑持续盈利，仍是市场关注的核心问题。前三季度研发、销售、管理费用分别为7.85亿元、4.23亿元、1.64亿元，三项费用合计约13.72亿元，规模和同期药品销售收入14.49亿元接近，这也意味着，在剔除BD收入后，诺诚健华内生商业化盈利压力不小。傅欣对此进一步表示，公司2026年第三季度实现持续盈利，2026年1—9月与上年同期相比扭亏为盈。但从目前收入结构来看，BD收入对公司业绩增长形成了较为明显的支撑，药品销售能否在覆盖相关费用后持续支撑盈利，仍待后续观察。二、奥布替尼贡献超九成商业化收入药品销售收入持续增长的背后，是诺诚健华对于奥布替尼这一核心产品的依赖。 2025年，诺诚健华商业化产品收入约14.42亿元，同比增长43.43%，其中，奥布替尼贡献收入14.10亿元，占比约97.78%。进入2026年，诺诚健华预计2026年全年药品销售收入增速有望超过35%，但目前公开资料未披露奥布替尼具体销售额。从药品销售收入来看，2026年前三季度，公司药品销售收入同比增长41.47%。在半年报中，诺诚健华将奥布替尼销售增长的驱动因素归结为一线适应症获批、医保覆盖扩大目标患者群体、差异化适应症定位，以及商业化团队持续提升市场渗透率等。不过，奥布替尼所在的BTK抑制剂市场竞争激烈。2025年医保目录调整后，包含奥布替尼在内已有五款BTK抑制剂纳入国家医保。诺诚健华在半年报中也表示，相关治疗领域已有多款获批产品及处于临床研究阶段的竞品，伊布替尼、泽布替尼等产品在中国的获批上市和纳入医保时间均早于奥布替尼，公司在市场推广方面面临一定竞争压力。对于BTK抑制剂国内目前的竞争格局，10月27日摩熵数科分析师向时代周报记者表示，据摩熵医药销售数据库，从医院端、实体药店及网上药店销售数据看，百济神州的泽布替尼2025年销售额达25.61亿元，2021—2025年年复合增长率为39.5%，占据较大市场份额；奥布替尼2025年销售额达10.02亿元，2021—2025年年复合增长率超过80.7%，放量速度较快，但市场份额仍需追赶。图源：摩熵医药-全终端销售数据库同时，上述分析师表示，随着国产BTK抑制剂陆续纳入医保，价格下降已经成为必然。行业竞争已经从市场抢占转向临床价值优势、医保支付覆盖、一线治疗获批等综合因素的竞争。这也意味着，尽管奥布替尼仍处于快速放量期，但诺诚健华对单一核心产品的依赖仍较为突出。目前，诺诚健华也正推动其他商业化产品逐步放量。公司执行董事、董事会主席兼行政总裁崔霁松在业绩发布会上表示，坦昔妥单抗于2026年迎来首个完整销售年度，预计将持续进行商业化贡献；佐来曲替尼为公司首款获批上市的实体瘤治疗药物，且儿科适应症的上市申请正在推进中，有望进一步覆盖更多患者人群。不过，与奥布替尼相比，上述产品目前收入贡献仍较为有限，能否随着商业化推进逐步放量，成为公司新的收入支柱，仍有待观察。 仿制药 行业政策法规 创新药/改良型新药 26页 免费下载 1.4.1 本周全球TOP10创新药研发进展（1）GSK乙肝治愈药物Hibsago获 FDA 批准上市10月20日，GSK宣布，其下反义寡核苷酸（ASO）创新药 Hibsago（bepirovirsen，贝普若韦生）已获得美国FDA正式批准上市，与核苷（酸）类似物逆转录酶抑制剂（NrtI）联合用于治疗慢性乙型肝炎（CHB）病毒感染。今年8月，Hibsago在日本首次获批，成为日本首个获批用于实现慢性乙肝功能性治愈的治疗方案。Bepirovirsen最初由Ionis Pharmaceuticals发现。2019年，GSK从Ionis获得了该药物的全球开发和商业化权利。本次获批基于B-Well 3期临床项目的积极结果，该项目包括B-Well 1和B-Well 2两项研究。此前发布的汇总数据显示，在基线HBsAg水平≤3000 IU/mL的成人患者中，bepirovirsen联合标准治疗实现了19%的功能性治愈应答率，而安慰剂联合标准治疗组的这一比例为0%。FDA曾授予bepirovirsen突破性疗法认定。（2）诺华在研放射性配体疗法拟纳入突破性治疗品种10月21日，CDE官网显示，诺华（Novartis）申报的[225Ac]Ac-PSMA-617注射液拟纳入突破性治疗品种，拟用于治疗接受过雄激素受体通路抑制剂（ARPI）和紫杉类化疗且在[177Lu]Lu-PSMA靶向治疗期间或治疗后出现进展的前列腺特异性膜抗原（PSMA）阳性转移性去势抵抗性前列腺癌（mCRPC）成人患者。公开资料显示，225Ac-PSMA-617是一种在研的基于锕同位素的放射配体疗法（RLT），利用已验证的配体靶向PSMA，将短射程、高能量的α粒子辐射直接递送至前列腺癌细胞，诱导肿瘤细胞DNA链断裂实现肿瘤细胞杀伤，同时尽可能减少周围健康组织暴露。（3）进口肝病新药依非兰诺片在中国申报上市10月21日，CDE官网显示，益普生按注册分类5.1类申报的依非兰诺片国内上市申请获受理。早前，8月19日，该药已纳入优先审评，拟定适应症为：与熊去氧胆酸（UDCA）联合治疗对UDCA应答不足的成年患者的原发性胆汁性胆管炎（PBC），或在无法耐受UDCA的患者中用作单药治疗。据公开资料显示，依非兰诺（Elafibranor片）是一款新型的口服PPARα/δ双重激动剂，每日一次。2024年6月，依非兰诺率先在美国获批，成为近十年来首个获批用于治疗罕见肝病PBC的新药。该批准主要基于III期ELATIVE研究数据。与安慰剂联合UDCA组（n=53）相比，依非兰诺联合UDCA组（n=108）达到生化应答复合主要终点的患者比例高出13倍（分别为51%和4%，治疗差异达47%）。（4）伦康依隆妥单抗第四个适应症上市申请获CDE受理10月21日，CDE官网显示，百利天恒自主研发的全球首创(First-in-class)、新概念(New concept)、目前全球首个且唯一获批上市的双抗ADC 伦康依隆妥单抗（宜泽康®，BL-B01D1/iza-bren），治疗既往接受过内分泌治疗且在晚期疾病阶段接受过至少一线化疗的不可切除或转移性的HR+HER2-乳腺癌的药品上市申请（NDA）已获得正式受理。这是伦康依隆妥单抗继鼻咽癌、食管鳞癌、三阴性乳腺癌后，获CDE受理的第四项上市申请。本次新增适应症的上市申请，是基于伦康依隆妥单抗在HR+HER2-乳腺癌的Ⅲ期临床试验（研究方案编号：BL-B01D1-306）的期中分析结果。2026年8月，经独立数据监查委员会（iDMC）判断，该研究在预设的期中分析中达到无进展生存期（PFS）主要终点，成为伦康依隆妥单抗第5个达到主要终点的Ⅲ期临床研究，也是全球首个双抗ADC药物在HR+HER2-乳腺癌治疗中达到主要终点的Ⅲ期临床研究。（5）阿斯利康/第一三共重磅ADC新适应症在中国获批上市10月22日，阿斯利康宣布，其与第一三共共同开发与商业化的 优赫得®（英文商品名：Enhertu®，通用名：注射用德曲妥珠单抗）于2026年10月20日正式获得中国国家药品监督管理局（NMPA）批准，单药适用于治疗既往接受过治疗或无满意替代治疗方案的不可切除或转移性HER2表达为IHC 3+的成人实体瘤患者。该适应症是基于单臂临床试验的结果给予的附条件批准。该适应症的完全批准将取决于开展的确证性试验的临床获益。本次获批是基于四项II期试验结果，其中包括三项全球研究：DESTINY-PanTumor02、DESTINY-Lung01、DESTINY-CRC02和一项中国研究DESTINY-PanTumor03，研究结果表明德曲妥珠单抗在多种实体瘤类型中均展现出具有临床意义的应答。值得一提的是，这是德曲妥珠单抗在中国获批的第十项适应症，也是国内首个获批泛肿瘤适应症的HER2靶向ADC。（6）强生双抗新药特立妥单抗在中国获批新适应症10月22日，强生宣布，其申报的特立妥单抗通过优先审评审批程序在国内获批一项新适应症，适用于既往至少接受过一线治疗的复发或难治性多发性骨髓瘤成人患者。特立妥单抗是一款可同时靶向BCMA和CD3的双抗。2022年8月，特立妥单抗率先在欧盟获得附条件批准，成为全球首款获批上市的BCMA×CD3双抗，随后该药又陆续在美国、中国和日本等市场获批。该药最初主要用于接受过多线治疗的复发或难治性多发性骨髓瘤患者，近年来则不断向更早治疗线次及联合用药拓展。2026年3月，美国FDA批准特立妥单抗的一项新适应症，联合达雷妥尤单抗皮下注射用于多发性骨髓瘤治疗。在中国，特立妥单抗于2024年8月首次获批上市，单药适用于既往至少接受过三线治疗（包括一种蛋白酶体抑制剂、一种免疫调节剂和一种抗CD38单克隆抗体）的复发或难治性多发性骨髓瘤成人患者。本次是该药在中国获批的第2项适应症。此次批准主要基于MajesTEC-9研究的积极结果。（7）瑞博生物在研1类siRNA新药RBD4059注射液获批临床10月22日，CDE官网显示，瑞博生物申报的1类新药 RBD4059注射液（vortosiran）获批临床，拟开发用于心房颤动患者的卒中预防。RBD4059是由瑞博生物精心研发的核心产品管线之一，是全球首款靶向凝血因子XI（FXI）的抗血栓siRNA候选药物。FXI作为内源凝血途径的关键分子，其在血液凝固过程中发挥着至关重要的作用。RBD4059通过特异性地靶向FXI的信使核糖核酸（mRNA），精准地抑制其蛋白表达和活性，从而有效地阻断内源性凝血途径的激活，达到抗凝血、抗血栓的效果。研究表明，FXI水平天然偏低的人群罹患血栓性疾病概率较低，且不会增加自发性出血风险。因此，FXI抑制已成为当前极具前景的潜在治疗手段，既能有效预防血栓形成，同时相较于现有抗凝疗法具有更高的安全性。（8）康方生物依沃西单抗又一适应症拟纳入优先审评10月23日，CDE官网公示，康方生物依沃西单抗注射液的一项新适应症拟纳入优先审评，适应症为依沃西单抗联合化疗用于局部晚期或转移性胆道癌的一线治疗。此次申报进展与Ⅲ期临床研究HARMONi-GI1取得积极结果有关。2026年8月，康方生物宣布，该研究在预设期中分析中达到总生存期（OS）主要终点，并达到无进展生存期（PFS）和客观缓解率（ORR）的全部关键次要终点。依沃西是康方生物自主研发的、全球首创PD-1/VEGF双特异性肿瘤免疫治疗药物。在中国，依沃西已经获批三项适应症，适应症包括EGFR-TKI耐药的nsq-NSCLC、一线治疗PD-L1阳性NSCLC、一线治疗鳞状NSCLC。（9）石药集团/和铂医药新药巴托利单抗获批上市10月23日，石药集团与和铂医药宣布，中国国家药品监督管理局（NMPA）已批准 恩力达®（巴托利单抗注射液，皮下给药，170 mg (1 mL)/瓶；商标持有人：石药集团）上市，用于治疗抗乙酰胆碱受体（AChR）抗体阳性的成人全身型重症肌无力（gMG）患者。此次获批基于一项在中国27家研究中心开展的关键性3期临床研究的积极结果。巴托利单抗是一款靶向新生儿Fc受体（FcRn）的全人源单克隆抗体，通过阻断FcRn介导的免疫球蛋白G（IgG）抗体再循环，加速致病性IgG自身抗体的降解，为包括gMG在内的自身免疫性疾病提供了一种靶向治疗方法。巴托利单抗最初由HanAll Biopharma开发，于2017年通过一项战略合作与许可协议授权给和铂医药。根据和铂医药与石药集团子公司恩必普药业于2022年10月签订的许可协议，巴托利单抗在大中华区（中国大陆、香港、澳门和台湾地区）的商业化将由石药集团子公司负责，和铂医药将根据其在大中华区的年度净销售额获得分级特许权使用费。（10）启元生物QY201片正式纳入国家药监局突破性治疗药物程序10月23日，启元生物宣布，公司自主研发核心创新产品QY201片，正式被中国国家药监局药品审评中心（CDE）纳入突破性治疗品种，适应症为成人中重度特应性皮炎（AD）。QY201片是启元生物自研的新一代高选择性JAK1/TYK2双靶点抑制剂。药物通过阻断JAK-STAT炎症信号通路，下调多种关键促炎因子，实现皮损改善、快速缓解瘙痒的治疗效果。QY201 用于中重度特应性皮炎的 Ⅱ 期临床试验已顺利完成，成功达成主要研究终点，安全性与耐受性表现良好。目前项目已进入 Ⅲ 期关键性注册临床阶段。该项多中心、随机、双盲、安慰剂对照研究由北京大学人民医院牵头，已入组 461 例受试者，主要终点为第 16 周EASI-75 应答率与 IGA 应答率。1.4.2 本周全球TOP10积极/失败临床结果（1）吉利德口服α4β7整合素抑制剂emvistegrast临床2期成功10月19日，吉利德科学公布了口服α4β7整合素抑制剂 emvistegrast（GS-1427）治疗溃疡性结肠炎（UC）II期SWIFT临床数据。该研究将中重度活动性UC患者随机分配至不同治疗组，每日一次口服25 mg、75 mg或200 mg emvistegrast，或接受安慰剂治疗。在200 mg高剂量组的59例患者中，第12周有33例达到临床应答，比例为66%；安慰剂组60例患者中有22例达到临床应答，比例为37%（名义P值＜0.001）。其他疗效指标方面，200 mg content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 26, 2026 Bristol Myers Squibb Discloses Patient Death in CAR-T Multiple Sclerosis Trial Author(s)Nicholas Jacobus Bristol Myers Squibb discloses results from it's Phase I Breakfree-2 trial of CAR-T therapy zola-cel for multiple sclerosis. Advertisement Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) has disclosed a patient death in its early-stage Breakfree-2 trial studying zolacabtagene autoleucel, an investigational, autologous CD19-directed CAR T cell therapy, in patients with relapsing or progressive forms of multiple sclerosis (MS).The death was disclosed as part of a broader data readout presented in an oral presentation at MSToronto 2026 and follows the company’s decision to place a voluntary pause on zola-cel studies back in September.What happened to the patient?The patient, who had highly active relapsing MS, died of septic pneumonia one day after receiving high-dose chemotherapy and 44 days after zola-cel infusion.1 According to BMS, the patient experienced late-onset, non-ICANS motor symptoms following infusion that did not resolve with intermittent corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulin.Although the patient’s CAR-T cell expansion was consistent with that observed across the study, physicians administered high-dose cyclophosphamide, after which the patient developed septic pneumonia and died the following day. A BMS spokesperson told Reuters, “The patient had a late onset side effect, a series of other complications and was heavily pretreated prior to CAR T, confounding our ability to determine the root cause of the issue.”2 BMS says the death was unrelated to the earlier voluntary pause and that no additional Grade 5 events have occurred across any zola-cel autoimmune disease program, which has treated 190 patients in Phase I studies to date. Immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome occurred in 7.6% of patients (5 of 66), mostly Grade 1 or 2 and resolving in a median of two days; one Grade 4 case occurred in a progressive MS patient and resolved within four days after treatment with corticosteroids and anakinra.1 BMS says the majority of adverse events were brief and reversible, consistent with previously reported zola-cel data.On efficacy, all patients treated at dose level 2 (60 of 60) remained off disease-modifying therapies at last follow-up, including nine patients followed for more than 12 months.1 Among evaluable patients at dose level 2 with at least 26 weeks of follow-up, six of seven relapsing MS patients met criteria for no evidence of disease activity, and 22 of 24 progressive MS patients showed stability or improvement in disability progression despite prior worsening at baseline.BMS frames the data as supportive of zola-cel’s broader potential despite the fatality. “BMS is at the forefront of cell therapy science, pioneering a new era by exploring the potential for immune reset in patients living with autoimmune diseases,” says Lynelle B. Hoch, president of the Cell Therapy Organization at Bristol Myers Squibb. “The Breakfree-2 data demonstrate clinical potential for zola-cel in multiple sclerosis, showcasing the opportunity for treatment-free remission in patients who have depended on chronic therapies for years.”Jeffrey A. Cohen, professor of neurology and staff physician at the Cleveland Clinic’s Mellen Center, offers a more measured outside assessment. “These data suggest that CD19-directed CAR-T cell therapy may offer a new approach to treating multiple sclerosis,” he says. “While more research is needed, the potential to control relapses, stabilize disability and reduce reliance on disease-modifying medications is encouraging.”What’s next?With BMS now coordinating directly with the FDA on a restart timeline targeting early 2027, the company’s ability to resolve outstanding safety questions will likely determine how quickly, and how broadly, zola-cel can advance toward later-stage development in MS and other autoimmune diseases.SourcesBristol Myers Squibb Presents Results from Phase 1 Breakfree-2 Study of Zolacabtagene Autoleucel (BMS-986353) in Patients with Highly Active Relapsing and Progressive Forms of Multiple Sclerosis at MSToronto 2026 Bristol Myers Squibb October 23, 2026, https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261022949204/en/Bristol-Myers-Squibb-Presents-Results-from-Phase-1-Breakfree-2-Study-of-Zolacabtagene-Autoleucel-BMS-986353-in-Patients-with-Highly-Active-Relapsing-and-Progressive-Forms-of-Multiple-Sclerosis-at-MSToronto-2026Bristol Myers discloses patient death in early-stage cell therapy study Reuters October 23, 2026, https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/bristol-myers-discloses-patient-death-early-stage-cell-therapy-study-2026-10-23/ Newsletter Lead with insight with the Pharmaceutical Executive newsletter, featuring strategic analysis, leadership trends, and market intelligence for biopharma decision-makers. title: Your Questions Answered: Foundayo’s EU Panel Backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s Masked TCE Bet, FDA’s Rare Disease Overhaul, and More
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 19, 2026 Your Questions Answered: Foundayo’s EU Panel Backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s Masked TCE Bet, FDA’s Rare Disease Overhaul, and More Foundayo’s EU backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s masked TCE deal, FDA’s rare disease reset, and Bausch + Lomb’s new interim CEO — explained. Advertisement Lilly’s Foundayo Receives Positive CHMP Opinion for EuropeWhat did the EMA committee recommend?The European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use recommended granting marketing authorization in the EU for Foundayo (orforglipron) for two indications: weight management in adults with obesity or overweight, and the treatment of type 2 diabetes in adults whose blood glucose is not adequately controlled. The European Commission makes the final approval decision and typically follows CHMP recommendations within a few weeks.What is Foundayo and why does it matter?Foundayo is Eli Lilly’s oral GLP-1 receptor agonist — a once-daily pill that can be taken at any time of day without food and water restrictions. That last point distinguishes it from other oral GLP-1 therapies currently on the market. The drug received FDA approval for obesity in April 2026 and launched commercially in the United States in the second quarter. Lilly has submitted orforglipron for regulatory review in approximately 40 markets globally.The Stories Covered in this PieceEMA Panel Backs Lilly’s Foundayo for Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes in EuropeFDA Approves Enspryng (Satralizumab) for Thyroid Eye DiseaseAstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 BillionFDA Launches Rare Disease Framework InitiativeVir Biotechnology Enters R&D Collaboration with Gilead for Three Novel PRO-XTEN Dual Masked T-Cell EngagersBausch + Lomb Appoints Thomas Appio as Interim CEOWhat does this mean competitively?If the European Commission approves Foundayo, it would become the second oral GLP-1 available in the EU for weight management, following Novo Nordisk’s Wegovy pill, which received European approval in July for weight management only. In the type 2 diabetes setting, Foundayo would compete with Novo’s Rybelsus brand of oral semaglutide, which has been on the European market since 2020 and has grown into a multi-billion-dollar franchise. The CHMP recommendation opens a new competitive front between Lilly and Novo Nordisk in Europe’s oral GLP-1 market, adding to their existing rivalry in injectable incretin therapies.What did the clinical evidence show?The weight management recommendation is based on two studies involving more than 4,740 adults with obesity or overweight. The type 2 diabetes recommendation is based on four studies involving 3,765 adults compared against placebo, dapagliflozin, and oral semaglutide.FDA Approves Enspryng for Thyroid Eye DiseaseWhat was approved?The FDA approved Enspryng (satralizumab), an interleukin-6 receptor inhibitor developed by Roche, for adults with thyroid eye disease on October 16. Roche describes it as the first subcutaneous therapy for the condition — one that patients or caregivers can administer at home after training from a healthcare provider. It is Enspryng’s second indication; the drug was first approved in 2020 for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.What did the clinical trials show?The approval rests on two identically designed Phase 3 trials, SatraGO-1 and SatraGO-2, which enrolled 258 adults across 19 countries. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients with active, moderate-to-severe disease who achieved at least a 2 mm reduction in proptosis — eye bulging — at week 24. Results diverged: SatraGO-2 met its endpoint, with 52.9% of Enspryng-treated patients achieving a proptosis response versus 23.4% on placebo, and 60.7% showing reduced double vision versus 25.8%. SatraGO-1 did not reach statistical significance, with researchers attributing the gap to an unexpectedly high placebo response.How does this change the treatment landscape?Two disease-specific therapies were already approved — Tepezza and, more recently, Lumvoa — both administered by intravenous infusion. Enspryng’s subcutaneous, every-four-week maintenance dosing offers a different treatment experience, with the key benefit being reduced logistical burden rather than a demonstrated efficacy advantage over existing options. No head-to-head comparison with approved therapies was conducted.What are the remaining unknowns?Roche did not disclose pricing or launch timing. Long-term data beyond week 24 were not described in available sources. Separately, the FDA has granted priority review to a supplemental Enspryng application for myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease, with a decision expected in January 2027. Insitro will receive $40 million upfront and is eligible for up to approximately $1.46 billion in development and commercial milestones, plus single-digit royalties on global sales.What is insitro’s platform?Insitro’s Virtual Human platform combines large-scale human and cellular data with AI-enabled target identification and medicine design. The company was founded in 2018 and reports more than $750 million in capital raised, with existing collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb, Lilly and Gilead. It has nine programs in development, including genetic regulators of liver fat and fibrosis expected to enter the clinic in early 2027.Why MASH and cardiomyopathies?Both conditions are characterized by disease heterogeneity — a single diagnostic label covering patients whose underlying biology differs — which has complicated treatment development. In MASH, the FDA approved its first treatment, resmetirom (Rezdiffra), in March 2024, but the condition still lacks therapeutic options for most of the estimated 6 to 8 million US patients with moderate-to-advanced liver scarring. The cardiomyopathy scope was not specified in the announcement.What are the limitations of this deal?No drug candidates were named in the announcement. The collaboration sits at the discovery stage, with targets identified through AI-driven analysis still requiring validation through preclinical and clinical work. The $40 million upfront represents less than 3% of the total headline value, and neither company disclosed timelines for milestone payments.FDA Launches Rare Disease Framework InitiativeWhat is the Rare Disease Framework Initiative?The FDA announced a new effort to redesign how drugs and biologics for rare diseases are developed and reviewed. The initiative, outlined in a white paper released by the agency’s Rare Disease Innovation Hub, aims to build a regulatory framework tailored to the realities of small patient populations — covering clinical development, evidence standards, manufacturing review, and the role of patient voice throughout the process.Why is FDA doing this now?Despite years of regulatory flexibility programs for rare diseases, only approximately 5% of rare conditions currently have an FDA-approved treatment. The agency says that gap reflects the need for a more fundamentally tailored approach rather than incremental adjustments to a framework originally designed for common diseases.What are the specific commitments?The initiative outlines six priority areas: greater clarity and predictability in regulatory decision-making through tailored guidance; embedding the patient voice early and at defined milestones; leveraging external expertise for customized review; building shared institutional knowledge; applying risk-based approaches to manufacturing and pre-approval inspections; and championing innovative statistical approaches in rare disease development.What happens next?The FDA is hosting a public meeting on October 28 at its White Oak campus, facilitated by the Reagan-Udall Foundation, to gather input from patients, disease advocates, industry, and other stakeholders. Additional sector-specific roundtables and requests for information will follow. The detailed framework development — which could include new guidance, regulatory changes, and organizational changes within FDA — will be informed by that input.Gilead and Vir Biotechnology Enter $1.87 Billion Masked T-Cell Engager CollaborationWhat are the two companies agreeing to develop?Vir Biotechnology will discover and optimize three novel PRO-XTEN dual-masked T-cell engager development candidates for Gilead, targeting selected solid tumor-associated antigens. Gilead holds an exclusive license to develop, manufacture and commercialize the resulting therapies. Vir will receive $90 million upfront — including $65 million in cash and a $25 million equity investment at a 30% premium — and is eligible for up to $1.74 billion in additional milestones and tiered royalties.What is the PRO-XTEN masking technology?PRO-XTEN is designed to keep T-cell engagers inactive in circulation until they reach the tumor microenvironment, where tumor-specific proteases cleave the mask and activate the drug’s cancer-killing mechanism. Vir’s PRO-XTEN approach directly targets those barriers. Kemny/Science Photo Library By Elaine ChenOct. 27, 2026 National Biotech Reporter Elaine Chen[email protected]Elaine’s stories explore the boom in new obesity treatments, new drug payment models, the ways companies are affected by FDA changes, and the emerging psychedelics drug sector. She co-writes The Readout newsletter, and co-hosts STAT’s weekly biotech podcast, The Readout Loud. You can reach Elaine on Signal at elaineywchen.70. Artiva Biotherapeutics said Tuesday that it’s winding down after two patients died in a trial testing its cell therapy for autoimmune diseases, the latest in a series of safety events that have emerged in a promising research field. One participant in the Phase 2 study died from a neurological complication after receiving the treatment, an NK cell therapy. Researchers determined the death was likely not related to the cell therapy itself, but to a chemotherapy that was given before the cell therapy, Artiva said. It’s standard to give patients chemotherapies before infusing cell therapies to lower the patients’ white blood cell count and make room for the new cells.Advertisement Related Story STAT Plus: Patient dies in Bristol Myers Squibb autoimmune CAR-T trial A second participant experienced sudden death about two months after treatment. Researchers determined that this was not related to any component of the treatment process, but the cause of death has not been determined, the San Diego-based company said. He is also the author of the morning Pharmalittle newsletter and the afternoon Pharmalot newsletter. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to another working week. We hope the weekend respite was relaxing and invigorating because that oh-too-familiar routine of meetings, deadlines, and the like has returned with a vengeance. But what can you do? The world, such as it is, continues to rotate. To nudge it in a better direction, we are brewing another cup of stimulation. Our choice today is butter pecan with a dash of raw honey. Best of luck accomplishing your goals today, and of course, do keep in touch. … Bristol Myers Squibb reported that one patient died after receiving its investigational CAR-T therapy in an early autoimmune trial, adding to safety concerns about a growing field of research, STAT notes. In a Phase 1 trial that tested the therapy in multiple sclerosis, the patient experienced motor symptoms that did not resolve with standard autoimmune treatments. They were then given a potent immunosuppressant, but developed septic pneumonia and died, Bristol said in a press release. In a subsequent statement, Bristol said this patient was treated for a series of other complications prior to receiving the CAR-T therapy, “confounding our ability to determine the root cause of the issue.”Advertisement A Roche drug billed as a potential blockbuster helped patients with a form of lung cancer that had spread live almost six months longer than two competitive medicines, Bloomberg News says. The experimental treatment, called divarasib, fared better than similar drugs from Amgen and Bristol Myers Squibb in a late-stage study. The drug was given to patients with non-small cell lung cancer that had spread, in part because of a genetic mutation, after other treatments, including chemotherapy. The findings could help divarasib become the treatment of choice for this type of lung cancer, in which a mutation called KRAS G12C drives the tumor cell growth. title: Corxel, an obesity drugmaker, to go public via SPAC deal
content: An article from Dive Brief // Obesity drugs Corxel, an obesity drugmaker, to go public via SPAC deal Armed with a $300 million financing and two GLP-1 and amylin-targeting medicines, Corxel is set to become the latest weight loss-focused company to join the public markets. Published Oct. 26, 2026 Gwendolyn Wu Senior Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Corxel U.S. will go public via a merger with the SPAC Amanat Acquisition Corp., the companies announced Oct. 26, 2026. Michael Santiago/Getty Images via Getty Images Dive Brief: Corxel Pharmaceuticals, a drug startup developing a pair of weight loss medicines, announced Monday plans to go public by merging with a special purpose acquisition company. The SPAC deal and concurrent $300 million private investment will help Corxel take CX11, a GLP-1 pill licensed from the Chinese drug developer Vincentage Pharma, into late-stage testing. In June, Corxel said CX11 helped participants in a U.S. Phase 2 trial lose an average of up to 11.5% of their body weight after 36 weeks while displaying a “favorable” gastrointestinal tolerability profile. The combined company will also advance a preclinical weight loss prospect directed at a different gut hormone known as amylin. A third drug licensed from Biogen and in development for acute ischemic stroke isn't part of the deal and will instead be housed in a parent entity. Corxel's backers made clear in subsequent talks that they wanted the company to have a "more dedicated focus," rather than pursue "two different tracks," said Kevin Xie, its chief financial officer, in an interview with BioPharma Dive. What followed was a split, with two obesity drugs being merged into a publicly traded entity and the rest of Corxel funneled into a still-private parent. “Both companies have separate development strategies and financing processes, so that’s more welcome news to the investors,” Xie said. Formerly known as Ji Xing Pharmaceuticals, Corxel launched in 2019 and once planned to develop a nasal spray for dry eye disease. It offloaded that therapy in 2024, the same year it acquired from Biogen most rights to JX10 and licensed CX11 from Vincentage. CX11 was already in human testing when Corxel struck that deal. Now it’s on the verge of a global late-stage study. Corxel reported positive late-stage data in May from a Chinese trial run by Vincentage. An international Phase 3 test could follow as soon as the first quarter of 2027. Corxel is pitching CX11 as a “differentiated, next-generation” therapy and an option for people who don’t stay on injectable GLP-1s. Though it is well behind first-to-market oral GLP-1s like Eli Lilly’s Foundayo and Novo’s Wegovy pill, Xie said CX11 may be appealing to people who need to lose 5% to 10% of their body weight and are classified as overweight, but not obese. (Around 31% of U.S. adults fit this description, according to one National Institutes of Health estimate.) Corxel is testing higher doses of CX11 in a Phase 1b trial in an effort to explore the drug’s “efficacy upside,” according to a statement. Additional data are expected in the first half of 2027.
